subject: computer-science
title: Computational Thinking: Foundations
welcome_lead: Think like a programmer before you write a line of code.
meta_desc: KS3 computational thinking: decomposition, abstraction, patterns.
final_note: Break the problem, ignore the noise, find the pattern.

concepts.def: A precise step-by-step method for solving a problem.
Ways to express an algorithm before coding.
Linear search (any list) and binary search (sorted list).
Ordering data, e.g. bubble, merge and insertion sort.
Breaking a problem into smaller parts.
Hiding unnecessary detail to focus on what matters.

walkthroughs.body_html: Making a game seems huge. Break it down: graphics, controls, scoring, sound. Each part is a smaller, easier problem.
A Tube map ignores real distances — that detail doesn't help travellers. Abstraction hides what isn't useful, leaving what is.
If you spot a repeating pattern, you can write one piece of code that handles them all. Patterns turn long jobs into short loops.
